claims.text: A PersistentVolume's reclaim policy (spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy) tells the cluster what to do with the volume after it has been released of its claim; the policies discussed are Retain and Delete.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Persistent Volumes > Reclaiming; reclaim-policy.sh line 10 at stage-3

claims.text: Dynamically provisioned PersistentVolumes inherit the reclaim policy of their StorageClass (StorageClass field reclaimPolicy); kind's default class standard has reclaimPolicy Delete. volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer delays creating and binding the volume until a Pod using the claim is created.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Reclaim Policy; Storage Classes > Reclaim policy; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/reclaim-policy.txt lines 3-6

claims.text: With Delete, deleting the claim removes both the PersistentVolume object (gone from kubectl get pv) and the associated storage asset.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Reclaiming > Delete; reclaim-policy.txt lines 18-20

claims.text: With Retain, when the PVC is deleted the PersistentVolume still exists and is considered Released; the previous claimant's data remains on the volume, and it is not yet available for another claim (manual reclamation needed).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Reclaiming > Retain; reclaim-policy.txt lines 18-20

claims.text: rancher.io/local-path honours reclaimPolicy Retain on a StorageClass: the PV of a deleted claim of retain-local stays with phase Released.

A released PV keeps spec.claimRef naming its former claim (the CLAIM column, from .spec.claimRef.name, still reads kept); Kubernetes does not bind a new claim to it, so a new claim of the same dynamic class gets a newly provisioned volume.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Retain, Binding; reclaim-policy.sh line 10, reclaim-policy.txt line 20

claims.text: Deleting a namespace deletes all objects in it, including its PersistentVolumeClaims; their PersistentVolumes (cluster-scoped) then follow their reclaim policy, so a Delete volume is removed.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Namespaces (deleting a namespace deletes everything in it); reclaim-policy.txt lines 22-26

claims.text: Argo CD with syncPolicy.automated.prune: true deletes a resource whose manifest is no longer in Git on the next sync; this applies to a PersistentVolumeClaim like any other resource; apps/staging.yaml has prune: true.
claims.source_hint: argo-cd docs: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Pruning; deploy/gitops/config-repo/apps/staging.yaml line 25 at stage-3

claims.text: retain-storageclass.yaml at stage-3: retain-local: provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer — same provisioner and binding mode as standard (kubectl get storageclass); standard is also the default class, retain-local is not.

reclaim-policy.sh at stage-3: data has no storageClassName; kept = copy of data-pvc.yaml plus storageClassName: retain-local; writer lists both as Pod volumes (L25-34); L41-45 delete writer, both claims, wait 10 s, list; L50-56 recreate data and writer, delete the namespace, list.
The volumes function lists PVs with columns CLAIM (.spec.claimRef.name), CLASS, RECLAIM (.spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy), STATUS (.status.phase), filtered to claims data or kept.
Output at stage-3: before deletion data (standard, Delete) and kept (retain-local, Retain) are Bound; after deleting the claims and after deleting the namespace only kept, Retain, Released is listed.
Deleting a Released PV object with local-path does not remove its folder on the node (script comment line 59); the cleanup below the excerpt deletes the Released PV and retain-local.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/reclaim-policy.sh lines 58-63 at stage-3; local-path-provisioner README

claims.text: In kind, a local-path volume lives in a folder inside one node container; deleting the cluster or losing the node loses it, Retain included. Stated only for kind (§6, §9); network storage can outlive the PV.
claims.source_hint: k8s.l2.storage-classes claims; kind docs: Configuration > Extra Mounts; deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml at stage-3

claims.text: A claim chooses its StorageClass with spec.storageClassName; the reclaim policy itself is not a field of the claim.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > PersistentVolumeClaims > Class; API reference PersistentVolumeClaimSpec

claims.text: A StatefulSet by default leaves its claims in place when it is deleted (taught in k8s.l2.statefulsets; the lesson says 'the object that made them' since StatefulSet is not yet known vocab).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: StatefulSets > PersistentVolumeClaim retention (default Retain for whenDeleted)

claims.text: Opinion: when data should rather be cleaned up by hand than lost to one mistaken delete, a StorageClass with Retain suits it; the cost is Released volumes that accumulate and need manual cleanup.
Opinion: Retain is not a backup — it keeps the single copy in place; a backup is a separate copy kept elsewhere.

beyond_scope: Released PV still names its old claim (CLAIM column) — only to explain output, no claimRef cleanup taught; local-path leaves the folder when a Released PV is deleted — from the script's comment
